form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Ms. McSally (for herself and Ms. Sinema) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

form.official-title: To amend the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 to establish an Aging Infrastructure Account, to amend the Reclamation Safety of Dams Act of 1978 to provide additional funds under that Act, to establish a review of flood control rule curves pilot project within the Bureau of Reclamation, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Water Supply Infrastructure Rehabilitation and Utilization Act.
Section 9603 of the Omnibus Public Land Management Act of 2009 (43 U.S.C. 510b) is amended by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: There is established in the general fund of the Treasury a special account, to be known as the Aging Infrastructure Account (referred to in this subsection as the Account), to provide funds to, and provide for the extended repayment of the funds by, transferred works operating entities or project beneficiaries responsible for repayment of reimbursable costs for the conduct of extraordinary operation and maintenance work at transferred works, which shall consist of—

subparagraph.text: any amounts that are authorized to be appropriated to the Account under section 9605; and
any amounts deposited in the Account under paragraph (3)(B).

paragraph.text: Subject to appropriations and paragraph (3), the Secretary may expend amounts in the Account to fund and provide for extended repayment of the funds for eligible projects at transferred works identified in a report submitted under paragraph (5)(A).

subparagraph.text: The Secretary may not expend amounts under paragraph (2) with respect to an eligible project described in that paragraph unless the transferred works operating entity or project beneficiary responsible for repayment of reimbursable costs has entered into a contract to repay the amounts under subsection (b)(2).

Amounts repaid by a transferred works operating entity or project beneficiary responsible for repayment of reimbursable costs receiving funds under a repayment contract entered into under this subsection shall be deposited in the Account without further appropriation.

Not less than once per fiscal year, the Secretary shall accept, during an application period established by the Secretary, applications from transferred works operating entities or project beneficiaries responsible for payment of reimbursable costs for funds and extended repayment for eligible projects.
A project eligible for funds and extended repayment under this subsection is a project that—

clause.text: qualifies as an extraordinary operation and maintenance work under this section;
is for the major, non-recurring maintenance of a mission-critical asset; and
is not eligible to be carried out or funded under the repayment provisions of section 4(c) of the Reclamation Safety of Dams Act of 1978 (43 U.S.C. 508(c)).

subparagraph.text: Not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this subsection, the Secretary shall issue guidelines describing the information required to be provided in an application for funds and extended repayment under this subsection that require, at a minimum—

clause.text: a description of the project for which the funds are requested;
the amount of funds requested;
the repayment period requested by the transferred works operating entity or project beneficiary responsible for repayment of reimbursable costs;
the financial justification for requesting an extended repayment period; and
the financial records of the transferred works operating entity or project beneficiary responsible for repayment of reimbursable costs.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall review each application submitted under subparagraph (A)—

clause.text: to determine whether the project is eligible for funds and an extended repayment period under this subsection;
to determine if the project has been identified by the Bureau of Reclamation as part of the major rehabilitation and replacement of a project facility; and
to conduct a financial analysis of—

subclause.text: the transferred works operating entity or project beneficiary responsible for repayment of reimbursable costs.

paragraph.text: Not later than 90 days after the date on which an application period closes under paragraph (4)(A), the Secretary shall submit to the Committees on Energy and Natural Resources and Appropriations of the Senate and the Committees on Natural Resources and Appropriations of the House of Representatives a report that—

subparagraph.text: identifies each project eligible for funds and extended repayment under this subsection;
with respect to each eligible project identified under subparagraph (A), includes—

clause.text: a description of—

subclause.text: the anticipated cost and duration of the eligible project; and
any remaining engineering or environmental compliance that is required before the eligible project commences;

clause.text: an analysis of—

subclause.text: the repayment period proposed in the application; and

if the Secretary recommends a minimum necessary repayment period that is different than the repayment period proposed in the application, the minimum necessary repayment period recommended by the Secretary;

clause.text: an analysis of the effect on the affordability of water of—

subclause.text: the repayment period proposed in the application; and

if the Secretary recommends a minimum necessary repayment period that is different than the repayment period proposed in the application, the minimum necessary repayment period recommended by the Secretary; and

clause.text: an analysis of alternative non-Federal funding options; and

subparagraph.text: describes the balance of funds in the Account as of the date of the report.

section.header: Authorization of Appropriations for the Reclamation Safety of Dams Act of 1978
section.text: Section 5 of the Reclamation Safety of Dams Act of 1978 (43 U.S.C. 509) is amended, in the first sentence, by inserting , and, effective October 1, 2019, not to exceed an additional $550,000,000 (October 1, 2019, price levels) before , plus or minus.

section.header: Review of flood control rule curves pilot project

paragraph.text: The term Bureau means the Bureau of Reclamation.

subparagraph.text: The term eligible works means a reserved works, or a transferred works for which—

clause.text: the flood control rule curve has not been substantially adjusted during the 10-year period ending on the date of enactment of this Act; and
the Secretary receives a request in accordance with subsection (c)(1)(A).

subparagraph.text: The term eligible works does not include—

clause.text: any project authorized by the Boulder Canyon Project Act (43 U.S.C. 617 et seq.);
any project authorized by the Act of April 11, 1956 (commonly known as the Colorado River Storage Project Act) (43 U.S.C. 620 et seq.); or
any project of the Pick-Sloan Missouri River Basin Program (authorized by section 9 of the Act of December 22, 1944 (commonly known as the Flood Control Act of 1944) (58 Stat. 891, chapter 665)).

paragraph.text: The term pilot project means the pilot project established under subsection (b).
The term Secretary means Secretary of the Interior.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall establish within the Bureau a pilot project to adjust flood control rule curves in accordance with subsection (d).

subparagraph.text: In order for an eligible works to be selected for inclusion in the pilot project, a responsible party shall submit a written request to the Secretary.
Not later than 30 days after the date on which the Secretary receives a request under subparagraph (A), the Secretary shall notify—

clause.text: each responsible party of that request, using lists maintained by the Bureau; and
if applicable, the appropriate Federal power marketing administration.

subparagraph.text: select 1 or more eligible works for inclusion in the pilot project; and
submit a list of those eligible works to—

clause.text: the Secretary of the Army;
the Committee on Natural Resources of the House of Representatives; and
the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources of the Senate.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall not select an eligible works for inclusion in the pilot project under paragraph (2)(A) if, not later than 60 days after the date on which the notice is provided to each responsible party under paragraph (1)(B)(i), a majority of the responsible parties submit to the Secretary an objection to the inclusion of the eligible works in the pilot project.

The flood control rule curve of an eligible works shall be adjusted pursuant to section 7 of the Act of December 22, 1944 (33 U.S.C. 709), if the Secretary of the Army determines that the adjustment would enhance the authorized purposes of the eligible works.
In the adjustment of a flood control rule curve under paragraph (1), the following factors shall be considered:

subparagraph.text: Forecast-informed reservoir operations.
Improved hydrologic forecasting for—

clause.text: precipitation;
snowpack;
runoff; and
soil moisture conditions.

subparagraph.text: Any new watershed data, including data provided by a responsible party for the eligible works.

paragraph.text: In the adjustment of a flood control rule curve under paragraph (1), the following entities shall be consulted:

subparagraph.text: Each responsible party for the eligible works.
In the case of an eligible works that produces power marketed by the Federal Government, the Federal power marketing administration that markets the power.
The Secretary.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall consult with the Secretary of the Army with respect to any action taken by the Secretary of the Army—

paragraph.text: pursuant to section 7 of the Act of December 22, 1944 (33 U.S.C. 709); and
that relates to the pilot project.

subsection.text: The Secretary or the Secretary of the Army, as appropriate, may accept amounts from responsible parties for eligible works to fund all or a portion of the cost of carrying out an adjustment under subsection (d), including a review or revision of operational documents (including water control plans, water control manuals, water control diagrams, release schedules, rule curves, operational agreements with non-Federal entities, and any associated environmental documentation).

paragraph.text: affects or modifies any existing authority to review or modify—

subparagraph.text: reservoir operations, including any existing forecast-informed reservoir operations at a facility of the Corps of Engineers, such as Coyote Dam; and
flood control operations; or

paragraph.text: affects or modifies any authorized purpose of any project carried out by the Secretary.
The pilot project shall terminate on the date that is 15 years after the date of enactment of this Act.
Termination of the pilot project under paragraph (1) shall not affect any flood control rule curve developed as part of the pilot project.
